entries.title: Die Rolls
entries.summary: Most actions are resolved by adding a Characteristic and an Ability to a die roll and comparing the total with an Ease Factor; the margin of success shows how well the action went. Magic uses the same basic pattern with its own totals.
quotes: the roll is normally Characteristic + Ability + Die Roll against an Ease Factor
If the total equals or exceeds the Ease Factor, the action succeeds.

entries.title: Simple Die
entries.summary: The simple die is a single ten-sided die read at face value, with a zero counting as ten. It is used when a roll carries no risk of spectacular success or failure.
quotes: Roll a ten-sided die. Each number counts for its value, except that a zero counts as ten.

entries.title: Stress Die
entries.summary: A stress die is rolled when a character is under pressure. A one is rerolled with the result multiplied up each time it repeats, and a zero on the first roll means checking botch dice to see whether the roll is a botch or simply nothing.
quotes: On a roll of one, roll again and double the number rolled.
On the first roll, zero counts as zero, and you must normally roll for a botch.
On a botch, your total for the roll is never any higher than zero, in addition to any other consequences.

entries.title: Botch Dice
entries.summary: Botch dice measure how likely a stress roll is to go disastrously wrong; the more that come up zero, the worse the outcome. The storyguide sets the number from circumstances, and a table gives the chance of a botch for each number of dice.
quotes: The base for most situations is a single botch die.
the chance of a botch can never be higher than 10%.

entries.title: Ease Factor
entries.summary: A table of standard Ease Factors from trivial to almost impossible, with notes on how likely characters of differing skill are to succeed at each. Storyguides use it to set difficulties for ordinary rolls.
quotes: Moderate skill is a score of 3 in an Ability, 'Skilled' means a score of 6, and 'Very Skilled' means 9.

entries.title: Abilities Overview and Ability Rolls
entries.summary: Introduces Abilities and the basic Ability roll: add a Characteristic and an Ability to a die roll and meet or exceed an Ease Factor, with the Characteristic chosen to fit the situation.
quotes: Abilities are normally used by adding Characteristic + Ability + die roll, and meeting or exceeding an Ease Factor.

entries.title: Specializations
entries.summary: Each Ability except Spell Mastery gets a specialization that raises the effective score when the specialization applies.
quotes: you act as if your score were one level higher than it actually is

entries.title: Abilities With No Score
entries.summary: Explains whether and how a character with no score in an Ability can use it, depending on whether the Ability is asterisked and whether any experience has been put in it.
quotes: she may use it as if it had a score of zero, but rolling three extra botch dice
Characters cannot use Supernatural Abilities unless they have at least one experience point in the Ability.

entries.title: Ability Roll (summary box)
entries.summary: Summary box giving the standard Ability roll, the use of unscored Abilities and the specialization bonus.
quotes: Characteristic + Ability + die roll, meet or exceed the Ease Factor to succeed

entries.title: Rounding
entries.summary: Where a rule involves division and does not say which way to round, the result is rounded down.
quotes: but if it does not, round down.

entries.title: Abilities
entries.summary: Abilities are learned skills in five types. Academic, Arcane and Martial Abilities need an appropriate Virtue or Flaw (or being a magus), Supernatural Abilities need a specific source, and Spell Mastery is for Hermetic magi only.
quotes: A character can only learn Academic, Arcane, or Martial Abilities if he has an appropriate Virtue or Flaw, or is a magus.

entries.title: Profession Herald
entries.summary: A new Profession Ability covering knowledge of the tournament circuit, heraldic devices, colors and deeds, tournament law, and locating tournaments in an area known by Area Lore.
quotes: The Ability Profession: Herald allows a character to recognize knights by their colors and heraldic devices

entries.title: Characteristics
entries.summary: The eight inborn Characteristics each have a score centered on average; they are fixed apart from rare drastic events or powerful magic.
quotes: All but the most exceptional of individuals have Characteristics that fall between -3 and +3.

entries.title: Characteristic Descriptions
entries.summary: Describes what each Characteristic (Intelligence, Perception, Strength, Stamina, Presence, Communication, Dexterity and Quickness) represents and which Abilities and activities rely on it.
quotes: Spellcasting relies on Stamina.
Your effective Quickness is usually modified by your Encumbrance.

entries.title: Encumbrance
entries.summary: Total Load from carried items determines Burden, and Strength offsets Burden to give Encumbrance, which is subtracted from many rolls though not from combat Attack and Defense when due to weapons and armor.
quotes: Burden increases when Load reaches the level for that Burden, so that a character with a Load of 9 has a Burden of 3.
If the character's Strength is zero or negative, his Encumbrance is the same as his Burden.

entries.title: The Grog Pack
entries.summary: Lists the equipment each grog carries on expeditions according to the liber gregis and states the Load of a pack, noting that it can be dropped without using an action so need not count in combat.
quotes: each grog pack imposes a Load of 4

entries.title: Encumbrance and Ability Use
entries.summary: Encumbrance penalizes physical activities and Fatigue rolls, but for climbing, swimming and balancing the storyguide uses Burden instead as the penalty to Ability rolls.
quotes: use Burden rather than Encumbrance as a penalty to Ability rolls

entries.title: Equipment Bonuses (optional rule)
entries.summary: Optional rule letting non-essential equipment reduce the Ease Factor of an Ability roll by a minor or major amount, with only one bonus per roll and matching penalties for poor equipment.
quotes: Minor assistance subtracts 1 from the Ease Factor, whereas major assistance subtracts 3.

entries.title: Encumbrance and Load
entries.summary: Converts Load to weight, gives the maximum weight a character can carry, lift, push or drag by Burden relative to Strength, the help from pulleys and levers, and how four-footed beasts calculate Encumbrance.
quotes: 1 Point of Load = 7 pounds
Burden equal to (Strength + 5)
Burden equal to (Strength + 12)

entries.title: Equipment Bonuses table
entries.summary: Example table of pieces of equipment, the Ability and specialty they assist, and whether the help is minor or major.

entries.title: Expanded Encumbrance Table
entries.summary: Table converting Total Load to weight in pounds and to Burden for heavy loads.

entries.title: Weight of Common Materials
entries.summary: Table of weights per cubic foot of common materials with how many cubic feet fit in a Target: Individual, plus a table converting Size to a weight range.
quotes: A +1 increase in Size doubles the weight

entries.title: Personality Traits
entries.summary: Short descriptors with scores that guide roleplaying; for magi and companions they are mostly memory aids, but for shared grogs they can be rolled with a stress die when unsure of a reaction.
quotes: If you do roll them, add nothing but the Personality Trait, and roll a stress die.

entries.title: Making Personality Trait Rolls
entries.summary: How to decide a character's action with a Personality Trait roll, how to treat opposed Traits and Personality Flaws, and how conflicting Traits shift the Ease Factor.
quotes: add the Personality Trait to the result of a stress die

entries.title: Personality Rolls
entries.summary: A table of suggested Ease Factors for Personality Trait rolls, with examples for Brave and Loyal and a general column for any Trait.

entries.title: Changing Personality Traits
entries.summary: Personality Traits can be changed freely by the controlling player, but only between sessions, to reflect events or exceptional rolls.
quotes: Personality Traits can only be changed by the player who controls the character, and only between game sessions.

entries.title: Personality Traits for grogs
entries.summary: Suggests troupes make greater use of Personality Trait rolls for grogs, gives the usual starting Traits (Brave and Loyal), and says a Personality Flaw can be matched with an extra Trait at a set value.
quotes: Most grogs should have a Brave and a Loyal Personality Trait.
This trait should have a value of +3 (for a Minor Flaw) or +6 (for a Major Flaw).

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.40

entries.title: Personality Flaws (treating as traits)
entries.summary: States how Personality Flaws are treated as traits when rules involve Personality Traits, so holy influence can oppose them.
quotes: treat a Minor Personality Flaw as a +3 trait, and a Major Personality Flaw as a +6 trait

entries.title: Ability Types
entries.summary: Lists the six types of Ability and notes that they are used alike, the difference being who may learn them.
quotes: There are six types of Ability

entries.title: General Abilities (type)
entries.summary: General Abilities can be learned by almost anyone with no game restrictions.
quotes: there are no game restrictions on who may do so

entries.title: Academic Abilities (type)
entries.summary: Academic Abilities need formal training, a Virtue or magus status for beginning characters, and usually a minimum score in a learned language.
quotes: Academic Abilities require formal training.
learning an Academic Knowledge normally requires a Latin, Greek, Hebrew, or Arabic score of at least 3

entries.title: Arcane Abilities (type)
entries.summary: Arcane Abilities may be bought at character generation only with a permitting Virtue or as a magus, and some Virtues also allow Penetration.
quotes: A character may only take these Abilities during character generation if permitted to by a Virtue, or if he is a magus.

entries.title: Martial Abilities (type)
entries.summary: Martial Abilities may be bought at character generation only with a permitting Virtue or Flaw, or as a magus.
quotes: Characters may only gain Martial Abilities during character generation if they are permitted to do so by a particular Virtue or Flaw, or if they are magi.

entries.title: Confidence
entries.summary: Important characters have a Confidence Score and a pool of Confidence Points to spend, with no cap on how many points can be held.
quotes: These characters start with three Confidence Points.

entries.title: Using Confidence
entries.summary: Confidence Points can be spent after seeing a roll to boost the total, up to the character's Confidence Score per roll. Spent points are gone for good, and they cannot be used on a botch or on whole-season rolls.
quotes: A player may spend Confidence Points on most rolls to get +3 to the total per point spent.
A player may spend any number of points up to, but not exceeding, the character's Confidence Score.

entries.title: Getting New Confidence Points
entries.summary: At the end of a session the storyguide awards Confidence Points to characters who played a significant part, one for each of a list of achievements such as reaching goals, succeeding at a difficult task or good roleplaying.
quotes: Typical characters should gain two or three Confidence Points per session.

entries.title: Raising Confidence Score
entries.summary: A Confidence Score rises only through long-term events that greatly build self-reliance, using a Tytalus apprenticeship as the baseline.
quotes: A character's Confidence Score can only be increased by long-term story events which greatly increase the character's self-confidence and self-reliance.

entries.title: Concentration
entries.summary: The storyguide may call for a Concentration roll before a demanding task or a retry after failure, and it helps magi hold spells through distractions.
quotes: the storyguide can call for a Concentration roll before you can make the attempt

entries.title: Size
entries.summary: Every character has a Size score; adult humans are usually Size 0, and each step represents a multiplicative change in mass. Size matters more for non-human creatures.
quotes: Every three points of Size represents a ten-fold increase or decrease in mass

entries.title: Stealth
entries.summary: Stealth covers sneaking, hiding and following people unnoticed, the latter rolled against the other person's Perception.
quotes: which is rolled against the other person's Perception

entries.title: Identifying an Artist's Work
entries.summary: Describes how production artists work for a select clientele and gives the rolls for recognising who made a piece of artwork, with artists identifying work more easily than non-artists and a higher Reputation making it easier still.
quotes: An artist character can identify an artwork's creator with a Perception + the creator's (Artist) Reputation + a simple die roll against an Ease Factor of 15.
Non-artist characters may identify a particular piece of artwork with a Perception + the creator's (Artist) Reputation + simple die roll against an Ease Factor of 18.

entries.title: Performers' (Profession) Ability and Picking Pockets
entries.summary: Explains when a performer uses his (Profession) Ability and when a general Ability applies, and when the Profession may substitute for a physical Ability such as Athletics or Brawl. Also gives the roll for performers who captivate a crowd while a thief among them picks pockets.
quotes: Dexterity + (Profession) Ability + stress die roll against an Ease Factor of 12
the thief gets a +3 bonus to his roll

entries.title: Minstrels Who Are Also Poets
entries.summary: A minstrel who is also a poet holds both a Profession Ability and a Craft Ability, using the Profession to set the Aesthetic Quality of a song and the Craft: Poetry to set the Aesthetic Quality of a written poem.
quotes: When composing a song, he would use his Profession: Minnesinger Ability to determine the song's Aesthetic Quality.

entries.title: Creating Art: Fame, Muses and Artist Reputation Goal
entries.summary: Introduces the artist's career arc in game terms: a successful artist attracts a muse, a supernatural patron who eventually carries him to a realm of immortality, and his (Artist) Reputation grows from the quality of his work, his benefactor's power and the praise he receives.
quotes: In game terms, every artist character strives to reach an (Artist) Reputation of 10, achieving various benefits along the way.

entries.title: Aesthetic Quality of Artwork
entries.summary: Every piece of artwork has an Aesthetic Quality, worked out from Dexterity plus a Craft Ability for production arts or Communication plus a Profession Ability for performance arts, then modified by listed bonuses such as Virtues, extra time, overtime, liberal arts knowledge, a muse and, for legendary artists, the local aura. A player may also gamble on experimentation, rolling a bonus die and then consulting the experimentation results.
quotes: Aesthetic Quality: Dexterity + Craft Ability + bonuses OR Communication + Profession Ability + bonuses
An artist can double the time it takes to create a piece of artwork and receive a +1 bonus.

entries.title: Artist Experimentation Results
entries.summary: A table and explanation of what happens when an artist experiments with a piece: results run from disaster and ruined artwork through no effect to the artwork or the artist being praised, affecting Aesthetic Quality and (Artist) Reputation.
quotes: The character gains experience points in his (Artist) Reputation equal to the Aesthetic Quality of the piece.
The art is so excellent that the artist gains enough experience points to raise his (Artist) Reputation score one whole level.

entries.title: Performing a Performance
entries.summary: A performer fixes the Aesthetic Quality of a routine, play or song when first creating it, and normally no further roll is needed. In unusual circumstances the storyguide calls for a roll, using the highest-skilled participant for group performances.
quotes: Communication or Dexterity + Profession Ability + stress die vs. Aesthetic Quality/2

entries.title: Gaining and Losing Artist Reputation
entries.summary: An artist character keeps a separate (Artist) Reputation for each Craft or Profession, which grows like an Ability from experience points earned specifically for it. The usual source is completing artwork of high enough Aesthetic Quality, with further lists of events that add or subtract Reputation experience points.
quotes: Aesthetic Quality greater than 3 times Artist Reputation = 1 Artist Reputation experience point
Gaining a patron grants 6 experience points
Losing a patron subtracts 12 experience points

entries.title: Benefits of Artist Reputation
entries.summary: Describes what each Artist Reputation threshold gives: a bonus to impressive social rolls, a minor muse, the right to sign work and a Confidence increase, a major muse, a permanent bonus to Aesthetic Quality, and finally legendary status. It also covers losing Reputation through truly deplorable behavior.
quotes: Once a character's Artist Reputation is 6, she can add +1 to any social roll in which her status would impress or influence a person.
the character does receive a 1-point increase in his Confidence Score when his Artist Reputation reaches 8
He gains a permanent +3 to the final Aesthetic Quality of his artwork, added on top of the normal calculation.

entries.title: Sponsors: Patrons and Benefactors
entries.summary: Every artwork needs a sponsor, either a benefactor for one piece or a patron for ongoing support. The artist spends a season rolling to find one, with modifiers by sponsor type and standing, increasingly wealthy sponsors required as Reputation grows, a ways to lose a sponsor, and a minimum payment when a player character sponsors an artist.
quotes: Finding a Sponsor: Communication + Bargain + Artist Reputation + stress die vs. 12 + modifiers
A player can make a Perception + Folk Ken + stress die roll against an Ease Factor of 12.
Cost to Sponsor an Artwork (Completed in One Season): At least 1 Mythic Pound per point of Artist Reputation

entries.title: Magically Created Art
entries.summary: Magi can create artwork instantly using the mundane-object creation rules, rolling Finesse to determine the Aesthetic Quality. Mundane artists cannot gain experience by studying such art, and intangible art needs Mentem magic.
quotes: Magically Created Art Aesthetic Quality: Intelligence + Finesse, –6, –9, –12, or –15

entries.title: Art of Memory
entries.summary: Memory-palace technique: the number of loci depends on the score, and a Complex Memorization roll against an Ease Factor lets the scholar remember a scene or writing in exact detail; those without the Ability can try with extra botch dice.
quotes: The character has a number of loci equal to five times their score in Art of Memory.
Stress Die + Intelligence + Art of Memory vs. Ease Factor of 9 (or higher)

versions.title: The Art of Memory
versions.summary: Introduces the Art of Memory, once a Mystery Ability but now a common academic Ability that any scholar can learn or take at character creation.
quotes: It has entered common knowledge and can be learned by any scholar

entries.title: Memorization Ease Factors
entries.summary: Table of Ease Factors for memorizing letters, conversations, rooms and buildings, with adjustments for length, technical material and substitute Abilities.
quotes: 9 (Average)
If the subject matter is highly technical add 3 or even 6 to the Ease Factor.

entries.title: New Ability: Art of Memory
entries.summary: Roll to memorize a complex scene or document perfectly, and the penalty rules for characters who lack the Ability.
quotes: Stress Die + Intelligence + Art of Memory vs. Ease Factor of 9 (or higher)

entries.title: Constructing a Memory Palace
entries.summary: Describes how a memory palace is structured, with five loci per room and a number of rooms equal to the Art of Memory score, and that memories can be deliberately forgotten.
quotes: The number of rooms in the memory palace is equal to the score in the Ability Art of Memory

entries.title: Personality Traits for the Four Complexions
entries.summary: Lists suggested Personality Traits associated with each of the four complexions, useful when choosing a character's Traits or reading a patient's complexion.

entries.title: Specialties for Medicine
entries.summary: Lists the areas that are suitable as Medicine specialties under the rules in this chapter.
quotes: diagnosis, prognosis, therapy, regimens, theriac, a specific disease

entries.title: Profession Apothecary
entries.summary: Describes the Profession: Apothecary Ability for identifying, growing and preparing medicinal ingredients, and the Medicine penalty when no medicinal supplies are available.
quotes: makes all Medicine rolls at a penalty of –3

versions.title: Profession Apothecary
versions.summary: Ability for identifying and preparing medicinal ingredients. Lack of proper medicinal supplies penalizes Medicine rolls and the patient's Recovery bonus, and a skilled apothecary reduces that penalty.
quotes: makes all Medicine rolls at a penalty of –3

entries.title: Specialties for Chirurgy
entries.summary: Lists the areas of practice that suit as specialties of the Chirurgy Ability under these rules.
quotes: the following areas are suitable as specialties in the Chirurgy Ability: surgery, surgical intervention, first aid, palliative care, midwifery

entries.title: The Craft Ability (Defined by Vocation)
entries.summary: Rules clarification that a Craft Ability is normally named by the character's vocation rather than by the material worked, with a survey of the materials common crafts use.
quotes: a craftsman should define his Craft Abilities by vocation rather than material

entries.title: Craft Specialization
entries.summary: Guidance on choosing a Craft specialization: a single item, workshop activity or quality of goods, giving a bonus to that narrow aspect of the Ability.
quotes: The intent of the specialization rules is to allow a character to gain a +1 bonus to a single aspect of a broader Ability.

entries.title: New Ability: Craft: Farrier (General)
entries.summary: Defines the Farrier craft Ability, how it can replace Animal Handling or Medicine for treating equine disease, and what quality of horseshoes high Craft Totals can produce.
quotes: the farrier has a +1 bonus to resolve it, increasing to +3 if it concerns the feet
A Craft Total of 12 makes Superior items, giving a +1 bonus for a single feature.

entries.title: Area Lore: The Hinterland as a Resource
entries.summary: How a character uses Area Lore to find people, resources and places in a city or its hinterland, with a penalty when searching away from where he usually lives.
quotes: Characters who spend most of their time in a city, like craftsmen, subtract 3 from Area Lore rolls to find material in the hinterland.

entries.title: Area Lore Ease Factors (table)
entries.summary: Sidebar table of Ease Factors for Intelligence + Area Lore rolls to know about shops, roads, inns, people, laws and hidden things, grouped by difficulty.
quotes: This is also the level required to contact most hedge magicians.
A person selling a service or product that is illegal, and actively repressed.

entries.title: Grammar: vocabularies and dictionaries as tractatus
entries.summary: Describes how grammar is taught and gives the one game rule in the section: vocabularies and dictionaries count as tractatus for the Latin Ability.
quotes: In game terms, dictionaries are equivalent to tractatus, the relevant Ability being Latin.

entries.title: Encyclopedias
entries.summary: Rules for treating encyclopedias as series of tractatus and for using them as a library for quick research: an hour's search, an Intelligence + Ability roll against an Ease Factor set by obscurity, with a bonus per relevant tractatus. Lists example encyclopedias.
quotes: treat every 5 books (or fraction) as a single tractatus on a given subject
each tractatus in an encyclopedia on the appropriate subject gives a +1 bonus to the Ability roll for that subject

entries.title: Format
entries.summary: Explains each line of the standard character write-up: Characteristics, aging and Warping, Confidence, combat, Soak, Fatigue, wound penalties, the Ability and Art notation with experience points, equipment, Encumbrance and spells known.
quotes: The format is Ability X(Z) (specialization), where X is the score in the Ability and Z is the number of experience points acquired towards the next level.

entries.title: Faerie Lore and What a Character Knows
entries.summary: Sidebar ruling that the Faerie Lore Ability covers understanding, bargaining with and predicting faeries regardless of whether a character uses the book's framework, and that no perspective is at a disadvantage in play.
quotes: The Faerie Lore Ability quantifies the character's capacity to understand the motives of, bargain with, and predict the actions of faeries.

entries.title: Guild Lore (Ability)
entries.summary: A new Organization Lore Ability covering a guild's rules and bylaws, used for checks about guild members, other guilds and trade matters, with suggested specialties.
quotes: Guild Lore is an (Organization) Lore Ability that covers the rules and bylaws of the guild.

entries.title: Languages in Germany and Mutual Intelligibility
entries.summary: Lists the Living Languages of Germany with their dialect specialties and gives penalties applied when speakers of related languages or dialects try to understand each other, with a worked example.
quotes: Same language, different dialects: –1 penalty to both speakers
High German vs Low German: –2 penalty to both speakers
High German vs East Norse or English: –4 penalty to both speakers

entries.title: Writing Systems and Artes Liberales
entries.summary: Explains that a character's Artes Liberales score also limits how many writing systems he can read and write, lists the writing systems of Mythic Europe, and describes how new systems are learned from a source.
quotes: Each point of a character's Artes Liberales score allows him to use one writing system, defined as a separate alphabet and script as well as a separate language.

entries.title: Legerdemain
entries.summary: Sleight-of-hand Ability whose use is detected by the target rolling Perception plus Awareness, with a bonus to spot particularly delicate moves.
quotes: The target of an attempt rolls Perception + Awareness to detect your actions.

entries.title: Artes Liberales and Literacy
entries.summary: Artes Liberales is the foundation of academic study and also determines how many writing systems a character can read and write.
quotes: For every point in the Ability, the character can read and write one writing system

entries.title: Arcane Abilities of hedge wizards
entries.summary: The hedge wizard Social Status gives access to the Arcane Abilities Finesse, Magic Lore and Penetration, and often a tradition-specific analogue of Magic Theory.
quotes: at least the Arcane Abilities Finesse, Magic Lore, and Penetration

entries.title: (Hedge Magic) Theory
entries.requires: Hedge tradition with a theoretical basis
entries.summary: An Arcane Ability covering the technical practice of a hedge tradition's magic; traditions without practitioners holding it are poor at innovation, new effects and teaching.

entries.title: (Organization) Lore for hedge traditions
entries.summary: A General Ability for the legends, history, structure and goals of each hedge tradition; membership is not required, and some traditions use it in initiations.

entries.title: Organization Lore: Folk Witches
entries.summary: The Ability covers folk witch effects, coven locations and reputations; its specialty is a home coven, with extra botch dice for covens farther away.
quotes: roll an additional botch die for every week's travel this coven is from the character's "home" coven

entries.title: Islamic Law and Theology: Islam (Abilities)
entries.requires: Muslim character with access to Academic Abilities
entries.summary: Two Academic Knowledges used by Muslim characters: Islamic Law, the Muslim counterpart of Civil & Canon Law, and Theology: Islam, the counterpart of Christian Theology, each with suggested specialties.
quotes: This is the Muslim version of Civil & Canon Law.
This is the Islamic equivalent of Christian Theology.

entries.title: Judaic Lore (Ability)
entries.summary: A Knowledge of Jewish cultural practice such as poetry, folklore and songs, which all Jewish characters have to some degree and may take from childhood experience.
quotes: All Jewish characters are versed in Judaic Lore to some degree

entries.title: Rabbinical Law (Ability)
entries.requires: Jewish character with access to Academic Abilities
entries.summary: The Jewish version of Civil & Canon Law, with suggested specialties.
quotes: This is the Jewish version of Civil & Canon Law.

entries.title: Theology: Judaism (Ability)
entries.requires: Jewish character with access to Academic Abilities
entries.summary: The Jewish equivalent of Christian Theology, with suggested specialties.
quotes: This is the Jewish equivalent of Christian Theology.

entries.title: Legendary Artists
entries.summary: Explains what happens to an artist who becomes a legendary artist: he becomes an immortal creature of his muse's realm with a Might score and powers based on his art, is vulnerable to Hermetic magic affecting supernatural beings, and can keep gained experience only by means of mnemonic artwork or a supernatural familiar.
quotes: He gains a Might score equal to two times his highest Craft or Profession Ability, and a number of supernatural powers equal to that same Craft or Profession Ability.
The piece of artwork must have a finished Aesthetic Quality equal to twice the number of recently gained experience points.
Each point of Might allows the artist to retain 5 experience points from study.

entries.title: Muses
entries.summary: Describes muses as supernatural patrons of any realm, divided into minor and major by Might. A muse can temporarily sacrifice some of its Might to grant the artist supernatural Virtues or powers, and the bond brings Warping to the artist.
quotes: A minor muse is any supernatural creature that acts as an artist's patron and has a Might score of 15 or less.
Minor muses may sacrifice 5 points of Might and grant the character a minor, supernatural Virtue.
The artist gains 1 Warping point a year from a minor muse and 3 from a major muse.

entries.title: Sign Language (Monastery)
entries.summary: A language Ability specific to a monastery or nunnery, with a fluency scale and defaults to the sign languages of related and unrelated houses at different penalties.
quotes: It defaults to an Ability in the language of other monasteries of the same order at –3

entries.title: Prophecies of the End Times
entries.summary: Rules for using prophetic texts as sources of lore: a character who can read the language but lacks the Ability may roll to find a specific fact, and each extra book on the subject helps at the cost of more research time.
quotes: It takes about an hour to find the information.
For every different book he has on the same subject, he adds +1 to the roll but requires an additional hour of research time.

entries.title: New Arcane Ability: Forest Lore
entries.requires: Arcane Ability; learned in a supernatural forest
entries.summary: Defines the Forest Lore Arcane Ability, its scope for home and foreign forests, how it is advanced, and a table of what each score of understanding allows.
quotes: Forest Lore can only be increased through practice, and the Source Quality is always equal to the strength of the forest's aura.
For example, a score of 4 (instead of 1) is required to enter communion with a foreign genius locus.

related.text: Walking the Path: Communion, Sacrifice and Fruit

entries.title: Nature Lore Supernatural Abilities
entries.requires: Supernatural Ability: Nature Lore / Forest Lore
entries.summary: Nature Lore Supernatural Abilities let a character interact specially with a natural feature such as a forest or river. A river version lets its holder find regiones and vis, speak with supernatural inhabitants and commune with the river spirit without Hermetic magic.
quotes: This allows him to find regiones and vis within the Danube, speak with supernatural river inhabitants, and commune with the river spirit, all without the use of Hermetic magic.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p.103

entries.title: Organization Lore: Knights Templar
entries.requires: Virtue granting Templar membership (or troupe permission)
entries.summary: A new General Lore Ability covering Templar rules, personalities, provinces, tactics, sign language and ciphers. Normally only available to characters who belong to the order.
quotes: This Ability also gives the character knowledge of the Templar sign language
Specialties: personalities, history, politics, tactics, sign language, a particular region. (General)

entries.title: Personality Traits, Sins, and Tempers
entries.requires: Divine-aligned characters and mystics (Sinful Traits and Tempers)
entries.summary: Groups Personality Traits into paired Sins and Tempers, lets a trait be annotated with its Sin or Temper, and explains that a trait's value counts negatively for the opposed one.
quotes: When dealing with opposing tempers or sins, treat the trait's value as negative.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.40 Sins and Tempers
